draft.title: How banks lend savings
card: A bank collects deposits from many savers and pools them into one large amount of money. Savers can still take out their money when they need it.
The bank lends part of this pool to borrowers, such as a family buying a home or a business buying equipment.
the reward the bank pays savers for keeping money with it.
the cost borrowers pay the bank for the loan. It is a higher rate than the one paid to savers. The gap between the two rates is how the bank makes a profit.
draft.remember: Banks turn many savers' deposits into loans, and earn profit from the gap between the two rates.

a.q: Why does a bank charge borrowers a higher interest rate than it pays savers?
opts: The difference between the rates gives the bank its profit
The higher rate lets the bank repay savers their deposits
Savers choose to accept a lower rate for the sake of safety
The government sets the borrowing rate above the saving rate
a.why: The bank earns money on the gap between what it charges and what it pays. Repaying savers is a separate matter, because their deposits are still theirs and the bank pays interest on them from its earnings.
a.clue: Think about how the bank earns an income from lending.

b.q: Jess deposits $2000 in a savings account at a credit union. Which describes what the credit union may then do with her money?
opts: Pool it with other deposits and lend to borrowers
Hand it to a borrower and pay Jess no interest
Hold it unused until Jess decides to withdraw it
Lend it to borrowers at a lower rate than Jess earns
b.why: Her deposit is pooled with many others, and the credit union lends from that pool. Lending at a lower rate than it pays savers would lose money, so that option is wrong.
b.clue: Remember what happens to deposits from many savers.

a.best: The difference between the rates gives the bank its profit

b.best: Pool it with other deposits and lend to borrowers
